conditions.name: Common Cold
conditions.advice: Common colds are usually viral and resolve on their own in about 7-10 days. Rest, stay hydrated, and consider warm fluids or a humidifier to ease congestion. Over-the-counter remedies can help with symptoms — check the label and follow the directions, or ask a pharmacist what's appropriate for you.
conditions.see_doctor_if: symptoms last more than 10 days, you develop a high fever, or breathing becomes difficult.

conditions.name: Influenza (Flu)
conditions.advice: Flu symptoms tend to come on suddenly and can include fever, chills, body aches, and fatigue alongside cough or sore throat. Rest and fluids are important; most healthy adults recover in about a week. Fever/pain relief options exist over the counter — a pharmacist can advise on what's suitable for you.
conditions.see_doctor_if: you're in a high-risk group (elderly, pregnant, chronic illness), symptoms worsen after initially improving, or you have trouble breathing.

conditions.name: General Fever
conditions.advice: A fever is your body's response to fighting an infection. Rest, drink plenty of fluids, and dress lightly to help your body cool down. Monitor your temperature periodically.
conditions.see_doctor_if: fever exceeds 103°F (39.4°C), lasts more than 3 days, or is accompanied by a rash, stiff neck, confusion, or severe pain.

conditions.name: Tension Headache / Migraine
conditions.advice: Tension headaches often respond to rest, hydration, reducing screen time, and relaxing the neck and shoulders. Migraines may also benefit from a dark, quiet room. Over-the-counter pain relief can help for occasional headaches — check with a pharmacist about what's right for you.
conditions.see_doctor_if: it's the 'worst headache of your life', comes on suddenly and severely, follows a head injury, or is accompanied by vision changes, confusion, or fever.

conditions.name: Sore Throat
conditions.advice: Most sore throats are viral and improve within a few days. Warm salt-water gargles, throat lozenges, and warm fluids like tea with honey can soothe discomfort.
conditions.see_doctor_if: it lasts more than a week, you have difficulty breathing or swallowing, a high fever, or white patches on the tonsils.

conditions.name: Indigestion / Upset Stomach
conditions.advice: Mild stomach upset often settles with small, bland meals, staying hydrated, and avoiding spicy, fatty, or heavy foods for a day or two.
conditions.see_doctor_if: pain is severe or persistent, there's blood in vomit or stool, or you can't keep fluids down.

conditions.name: Food Poisoning
conditions.advice: Focus on staying hydrated with small, frequent sips of water or an oral rehydration solution. Rest and reintroduce bland foods (like toast or rice) gradually as you feel better.
conditions.see_doctor_if: symptoms last more than 2 days, you see blood, you can't keep any liquids down, or you show signs of dehydration (very dark urine, dizziness, dry mouth).

conditions.name: Seasonal Allergies
conditions.advice: Seasonal allergies respond well to avoiding known triggers, keeping windows closed on high-pollen days, and rinsing off after being outdoors. Antihistamines are commonly used — a pharmacist can advise on options.
conditions.see_doctor_if: symptoms interfere significantly with daily life, or you notice wheezing or difficulty breathing.

conditions.name: Minor Cough
conditions.advice: A mild, isolated cough often clears up on its own. Staying hydrated, using a humidifier, and honey (for adults and children over 1 year) can soothe throat irritation.
conditions.see_doctor_if: the cough lasts more than 3 weeks, produces blood or thick discolored mucus, or comes with chest pain or breathlessness.

conditions.name: Fatigue
conditions.advice: Occasional fatigue is often linked to sleep, stress, hydration, or diet. Prioritizing consistent sleep and regular meals can help.
conditions.see_doctor_if: fatigue is persistent, unexplained, or accompanied by other symptoms like weight loss, fever, or shortness of breath.
